html:
Dong Son drums are large bronze drums made by the Dong Son culture of the Red River valley in northern Vietnam, from about the 6th century BCE into the first centuries CE.

They are cast in one piece, with a star at the centre of the top and rings of birds, boats with feathered warriors, houses on stilts and people pounding rice. They were used in rituals, perhaps for rain, and buried with chiefs. Drums were traded or copied across Southeast Asia as far as eastern Indonesia.

Vietnamese tradition links this age to the Van Lang kingdom of the Hung kings. Dong Son came to an end under Han rule. Modern Vietnam treats the drums as proof of an old civilisation of its own, older than Chinese rule, and the Ngoc Lu drum is a national treasure.
sum: Dong Son drums are large bronze drums made by the Dong Son culture of the Red River valley in northern Vietnam, from about the 6th century BCE into the first centuries CE.
